rationale: The question title fits qualified subgroup findings; reported post-hoc correction evaluations support the scoped generalization improvements.

rationale: M3 and unspecified datasets support transfer improvements, but not universal forecasting; sweeping first-work claims and future applicability exceed reported evaluations.

evidence: Anthropic-HH; gold reward model committee; over 25% low/no agreement; six qualitative unreliability sources; cleaned-versus-original dataset training experiments.

evidence: Neural-network classification with within-class isometric regularization; adversarial-attack robustness evaluation on MNIST.
rationale: MNIST adversarial evaluations support a local robustness improvement, not general neural-network robustness or categorical claims about learning unstructured data.

evidence: Deep linear residual networks: no spurious optima; ReLU expressivity when parameters exceed sample size; CIFAR10, CIFAR100, ImageNet comparisons against all-convolutional networks.
rationale: Linear-residual and parameter-rich ReLU theorems, plus three classification benchmarks, support identity parameterization's importance within the reported architectures.

evidence: Twenty LLMs on three MCQ benchmarks; option-position and token-bias analyses; PriDe estimates priors using permuted subsets of test samples.
rationale: A broad model comparison supports susceptibility to option-position changes; token-bias analyses and reported debiasing demonstrations address the proposed mechanism.

evidence: Offline RL experiments mentioned; no concrete tasks, baselines, numerical findings, or theorem conditions reported.

evidence: Graph-learning tasks and models mentioned; no specific benchmark, comparator, number, or theorem condition reported.
